description.narrative:
The humanitarian crisis in Gaza continues to deteriorate due to ongoing violence, infrastructure collapse, and severe aid restrictions. The ongoing war in the Gaza Strip has led to unprecedented levels of destruction and loss of life. Since 7 October 2023 and as of 3 April 2025, the MoH in Gaza reported that at least 50,523 Palestinians have been killed and 114,776 Palestinians injured. This includes 1,163 people killed and 2,735 injured since the escalation of hostilities on 18 March, —70% of whom arewomen and children. The first phase of the ceasefire, which began on January 19, 2025, initially facilitated a significant increase in humanitarian aid, reaching approximately 90% of Gaza’s population. The United Nations Relief and Works Agency (UNRWA) reported that, for the first time since the conflict began, large-scale aid delivery alleviated some suffering. More than 560,000 people returned to North Gaza. However, given the extent of destruction, humanitarian needs remain critical. The ceasefire faced challenges, particularly disputes over Gaza’s political future and aid delivery terms. In response, Israel reimposed restrictions on aid entry at the start of March 2025. On March 18, 2025, Israel resumed heavy bombardments across Gaza, killing 415 people, including many children. The blockade andongoing attacks have severely exacerbated shortages of food, medicine, clean water, and fuel. Vulnerable groups—especially children, the elderly, and the sick—are at extreme risk.
This action will focus on restoration and provision of basic WASH services in targeted communities in North Gaza and Gaza, contributing to the fundamental role in sustaining life and preventing public health risks.This action will increase the availability of domestic water byat least 800 cubic meters per day through the supply of a new generator that powers a water well which is Connected to the operational water network that will transport water to the targeted communities. In addition, the action will improve the hygiene conditions for 450 returnee Households through provision of hygiene kits.
AREAOF INTERVENTION: Locations: Beit Lahia, Bet Hanon, and Jabalia in North Gaza Governorate, and Gaza City

participating-org.narrative:
Oxfam Novib has been active in the Occupied Palestinian Territory/Israel (OPT/I) since 1982 and working with Palestinian refugees in Lebanon since the mid 1980s. It has built up a strong network of relationships with local NGOs and counts among its localcounterparts some of the largest and most professional NGOs in various sectors. It has accompanied these NGOs in their development from ad hoc volunteer groups to sizeable professional institutions with national outreach. At the same time the conceptualisation of the programme has evolved from three country programs in the early 1990s to a program for Palestinians in the Middle East (PME) working withPalestinians in OPT, Israel and Lebanon.
The programme has changed over the years with the establishment of the Palestinian Authority (PA) in the mid-1990s from a focus on support and service provision at a grassroots level and grassroots mobilization, to working towards influencing the establishment of the PA, its lawmaking and supporting building a democratic state # this involved supporting efforts of Palestinian civil society to build the basis for a democratic Palestinian state with room for civil participation, ensuring inclusion of vulnerable groups, refugees and women, and shaping its laws and systems. Oxfam Novib has also supported partners that are working on the provision of humanitarian assistance, response preparedness and conflict transformation. We have also supported partners in the provision of health services, access to quality education and gender justice.
